text:
maria: heads up — alert from our perf monitors: host-side latency for streaming /generate jumped. 95th is +40ms, p99 +120ms after the proxy change earlier today. traces point to request parsing/tokenization step on the host. anybody seen this?

sam: on it. can you paste an example trace or a flame sample? :eyes:

maria: pasted a tiny flame sample from perf: 
```
host:parse_request 55% -> tokenizer.tokenize 35% -> json.parse 20% -> io.read 15%
tokenizer.tokenize shows a lot of short invocations, spikes when upstream sends small chunks
```

jordan: my hunch: the proxy's new chunking/coalescing change is actually *splitting* bigger payloads into many small frames for streaming, which makes our host tokenizer restart state machine per frame. that overhead multiplies. seen similar with websocket framing before.

liz: can you repro locally with curl and chunked transfer? also confirm if gRPC streaming path behaves differently (http/2 might avoid the split).

maria: repro command we used: 
```
curl -X POST -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" --data-binary @large_prompt.json http://edge:8080/generate
```
with the current proxy config (chunk-size=512) median host parse-only time ~8ms -> with chunking median ~18ms and 95th worse.

sam: ack. i'll run a microbenchmark matrix: chunk sizes [256,512,1024,4096] against both http/1.1 chunked and http/2 grpc streaming to measure tokenizer hits and syscall counts.

jordan: quick idea: buffer coalesce in the edge proxy so host sees larger contiguous buffers, or change tokenizer to resume across frames without reparsing headers. second option is riskier.

liz: tokenizer is currently written around a full-buffer API: it assumes a single contiguous input. streaming support does incremental scanning but we do some expensive UTF-8 and punctuation heuristics that re-run at frame boundaries. short-term mitigation: coalesce to 4KB then hand to tokenizer. long-term: add a lightweight incremental tokenizer that keeps minimal state across frames.

sam: ran the first bench results: http/1.1 chunked at 512B -> host parse latency +9.6ms median; http/2 grpc stream -> +3.1ms median. coalescing to 4KB reduces median delta to +1.2ms. CPU samples show syscall/read spikes when frames are <1KB.

maria: thanks. can we get a quick patch to proxy to coalesce 4KB and roll to canary? i'd rather avoid a risky tokenizer rewrite during peak.

jordan: i'll draft the proxy revert/coalesce patch and add a feature flag `coalesce_chunks_bytes=4096`.

liz: also adding a small change to tokenizer: skip UTF-8 normalization on bytes that are mid-codepoint when we resume (cheap check). should cut the per-frame overhead a bit even if coalescing is enabled. i'll open a PR.

sam: test plan: microbench + unit tests for incremental tokenizer correctness, then canary on 3 hosts for 1 hour, collect p95/p99 and flame traces.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: proxy-config/coalesce-chunks=4KB on prod-edge-cluster-3 (3 hosts). monitor: /ops/infra/edge-canary.

maria: great — monitoring window 60m, but please annotate any regressions. i'll also add a perf regression alert for host parse time with lower threshold so we catch fallout. :thumbsup:

jordan: noted. follow-up tickets: EDGE-482 coalesce-bytes, RUNTIME-931 incremental-tokenizer-proof.

liz: one more note — if we decide to prefer gRPC streaming (http/2) we should measure request parsing CPU on the host process; initial numbers indicate it's cheaper because frames are bigger and fewer syscalls. might be a path for future optimization.

maria: cool. ok plan accepted: short-term coalesce in proxy + small tokenizer resume optimization. medium-term incremental tokenizer or gRPC-first routing. thanks all.
